# Badge

A compact, non-interactive label for metadata, with optional adjoining extensions.

## Usage

```ts
import { Badge } from '$lib/io/badge';
```

Use `text` for the primary label and `colorScheme` for its semantic meaning.
`extension` adds one segment; `extensions` adds multiple segments. False, null,
and undefined extensions are omitted. Each extension can override its color and truncation.

Use `truncate` inside a constrained container to shorten the primary label.

## Selection

Badges are small, non-interactive labels used to communicate status, categorize content, or draw attention to metadata. They appear alongside other UI elements and are purely informational — they do not trigger actions.

| Do                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Don't                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **USE-1** Keep labels short. One or two words is ideal. Badges are not sentences — "Active", "Pending review", "12" are appropriate; "Waiting for approval" is not.                                  | **USE-2** Don't make badges interactive. Badges communicate information; they do not trigger actions. If a badge needs to be clickable, use a Chip instead.                                                             |
| **USE-3** Use consistent labels across the product. If a status is called "Active" in one context, it should not be called "Enabled" or "On" elsewhere. Define a fixed vocabulary for status values. | **USE-4** Don't use more than one or two badges in the same row on a single item. Multiple badges compete for attention and dilute meaning. If an item needs many labels, consider an overflow pattern (e.g., +3 more). |
| **USE-5** Use status badges for system or workflow states. Things that change over time and reflect the condition of a record or process are well-suited to status badges.                           | **USE-6** Don't use color alone to convey status. Always include a text label. A green dot without a label is ambiguous to colorblind users and screen readers.                                                         |
| **USE-7** Use label badges for user-defined or editorial categories. Tags, content types, and taxonomy values fit the label variant.                                                                 | **USE-8** Don't use badges for user-entered free text of arbitrary length. If the content can be long or unpredictable, a badge is the wrong component.                                                                 |
| **USE-9** Use count badges sparingly. Reserve them for genuinely actionable counts — unread messages, pending tasks. Don't use them for decorative statistics.                                       | **USE-10** Don't invent new semantic colors. Use the defined color roles. Introducing ad hoc colors undermines the consistency that makes badges meaningful.                                                            |

## Rules

Checked against every PR that uses this component.

### Input

- **IN-1** `text` MUST NOT be empty. A caller with no value MUST omit the Badge.
- **IN-2** Each supplied `extension` or `extensions` object MUST contain nonempty `text` or a truthy `LeadIcon` or `TrailIcon`. An empty object still renders a segment.
- **IN-3** Callers MUST keep `text` in its natural case rather than uppercasing it in code; casing is presentation.

### Accessibility

- **A11Y-1** A custom icon-only extension MUST have equivalent text available to assistive technology, such as adjacent text that names the modifier. A hover tooltip alone is insufficient.

## Notes

How the component behaves. Context for reviewers; not checked.

- **BEH-1** `Icon` follows the primary text. Extension content is ordered `LeadIcon`, `text`, `TrailIcon`.
- **BEH-2** The singular extension precedes the plural extensions; false, null, and undefined entries are filtered out.
- **DIS-1** [`badgeRecipe` and `badgeSegmentRecipe`](./recipe.ts) own typography, colors, clipping, and truncation. Colors are applied to inner segments; the caller's `class` is applied to the outer RoundnessGroup.
- **DIS-2** `truncate` enables primary-label truncation inside a constrained width; extension truncation also depends on the extension's `truncate`.
- **BEH-3** Native attributes, including `data-testid` and accessible labels, reach the outer span. No test ID is assigned internally.

## API Reference

| Name        | Description | Type                                                                               | Default     | Required |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | -------- |
| text        |             | `string`                                                                           | —           | Yes      |
| colorScheme |             | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| "error" \| "accent"` | `"neutral"` | No       |
| size        |             | `"sm" \| "md"`                                                                     | `"md"`      | No       |
| truncate    |             | `boolean`                                                                          | `false`     | No       |
| Icon        |             | `false \| IconComponent`                                                           | —           | No       |
| extension   |             | `false \| BadgeExtension`                                                          | —           | No       |
| extensions  |             | `false \| BadgeExtensions`                                                         | —           | No       |
